root_cause_label: Incorrect Interpolation Order and Header Removal on Write-back
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent wrote a script at step 5 that applied ffill/bfill before linear interpolation (making interpolation inoperative) and saved CSVs without headers, and then never detected these logic bugs while spending steps 6-13 fixing an unrelated pandas API error.
t_err_evidence: In step 5 the script is written with two bugs: (1) ffill() and bfill() are applied before interpolate(), so linear interpolation has no NaN values to act on, and (2) df.to_csv(..., header=False) is used, stripping headers from the output CSV files.
t_commit_evidence: In step 13 the agent rewrites the final version of process_data.py; it fixes the pandas API issue and the CSV reading (adds header=0), but retains header=False on write-back and the wrong ffill/bfill-before-interpolate order. After this step only execution (step 14) and a completion claim remain.
t_surface_evidence: In step 12 a 'TypeError: Cannot interpolate with str dtype' appears because the header row 'water_level_m' was being read as data (not skipped), revealing the CSV was being read incorrectly. This is the earliest observable error signal related to the file-format handling bug.
trigger_explanation: The agent had a correct high-level plan (read CSV, interpolate missing values, save, count flood events), but generated code with two subtle logic errors: wrong ordering of imputation methods (ffill/bfill masking NaN before linear interpolation) and wrong to_csv argument (header=False removes the header). These are code-generation quality failures, not missing knowledge of the task spec or misread output.
forewarning_evidence: Steps 6, 8, 10, and 12 all produce TypeErrors when running the script (pandas API issues, then string dtype issue), signaling the script was not working correctly before t_commit at step 13.
